Badge.fix: Add `box-sizing: border-box;` to the `.md-badge` rule (badge.css:8) so `min-width: 16px` measures the border box and 4px inline padding leaves the kit's 8px label slot

Fix checks out: with border-box the 8px content slot holds "5" at 11px Roboto (~6.1px + 0.5 tracking) without clipping, and height is unaffected since padding-block is 0.

Reproduced both sides. KIT: /tmp/figspec/Badges__Badges.json, set `Badges / Badges`, variant Size=Large -> size [16,16], radius 100, pad [0,4,0,4], single TEXT child "Badge label" [8,16] chars "3" (4+8+4 = 16). Badge.summary: The large badge's pill radius is hardcoded as `border-radius: 8px` instead of the `calc(var(--_height) / 2)` pattern CLAUDE.md mandates for capsule shapes.
Badge.ours: `height: 16px;` (line 23) and `border-radius: 8px;` (line 25) as two independent literals, with no `--_height` custom property
Badge.kit: r=100 (fully round) on `Badges / Badges` Size=Large, i.e. radius = height/2 for a capsule that grows horizontally (see the 31x16 instance in `Menu / Building Blocks Trailing element`)
Badge.fix: Set `--_height: 16px;` on the `[data-size="large"]` block and use `height: var(--_height); border-radius: calc(var(--_height) / 2);` per CLAUDE.md's shape rule

verdicts.reason: Numbers are accurate but there is no defect. badge.css:23 `height: 16px` and :25 `border-radius: 8px` are literals, and the kit variant is r=100. But 8px IS 16px/2 — the resolved box already matches a fully-round 16px-tall capsule, and measurements.json confirms borderRadius "8px" on a 16px-tall element in every story. Per rule 3 the flaggable anti-patterns are hardcoded 999px / 9999px / var(--md-sys-shape-corner-full); 8px is none of those, and CLAUDE.md's stated rationale for the calc() pattern (9999px freezing morph transitions at visually-round intermediate values) does not apply to a literal half-height value, which interpolates normally. Badge also has no morph/shape animation to break. Literal half-height radii are the prevailing repo pattern rather than a badge-specific slip: navigation-bar.css:229 and :245 use `20px` on 40px-tall items, switch.css:69 `24px`, search.css:16 `28px`, slider.css:166 `22px`. Zero rendering difference from the proposed fix; this is a style-convention preference, not an actionable kit divergence.

Refuted — resolves identically and is an already-blessed deliberate choice. badge.css:23 sets height:16px and :25 sets border-radius:8px; 8 IS 16/2, so the rendered shape is exactly the kit's r=100 capsule for a 16-tall element (measurements.json reports borderRadius "8px" on a 16px-tall box — a perfectly round end cap). CLAUDE.md's rule bans `9999px` / `var(--md-sys-shape-corner-full)` for a stated reason: those break morph transitions because intermediate values stay visually round. A literal 8px has none of that failure mode, and Badge has no shape/morph transition at all (badge.css declares no `transition`). The repo already uses literal computed halves as its own idiom — src/styles/globals.css writes `--round-radius: 16px; /* 32/2 */`, `20px; /* 40/2 */`, `28px; /* 56/2 */` etc. And .design-sync/figma-audit.md:119-129 explicitly signs this off: "large radius | 8 (= height ÷ 2) ✅ | round ... a correct radius under the project's 'radius = height ÷ 2' rule". Introducing a `--_height` indirection changes zero rendered pixels; it is a style preference, not a defect.

Badge.summary: `.md-badge` hardcodes `font-weight: 500` on the root where the `--md-sys-typescale-label-small-weight` token already supplies it.

Badge.fix: Delete the literal `font-weight: 500;` at badge.css:12 and rely on the token already set in the `[data-size="large"]` block

verdicts.reason: Facts check out, defect does not. badge.css:12 is literally `font-weight: 500;` and badge.css:31 re-declares `font-weight: var(--md-sys-typescale-label-small-weight);` inside [data-size="large"]. But that token resolves to 500 (sys.typescale.css:120 `--md-sys-typescale-label-small-weight: 500`), and the kit agrees: Badges__Badges.json Size=Large label font is "Google Sans Text Medium" and `--var "Label Small"` gives Typescale/Static/Label Small/Weight = "Medium" = 500. measurements.json shows fontWeight "500" on both the large and the small badge. So the literal matches the token, the token matches the kit, and the rendered output is identical either way — nothing diverges from the design kit and nothing would change if the line were deleted. This is a code-tidiness nit about a redundant declaration, outside the scope of a kit-conformance audit, and it is inert for size=small anyway (badge.tsx:33 returns null content for the dot).

Refuted — zero rendered difference and no rule violated. `--md-sys-typescale-label-small-weight` is 500 (sys.typescale.css:120), so the token at badge.css:31 and the literal at badge.css:12 produce the same computed value; measurements.json shows fontWeight "500" for both size=small and size=large md-badge rows either way. The small dot renders no text at all (badge.tsx getDisplayValue returns null when isSmall, and BadgeProps Omits 'children'), so the root declaration is unobservable there rather than wrong. It also functions as a defensible fallback if a consumer blanks the typescale token. This is not a kit mismatch — the kit's own Size=Large label is "Google Sans Text Medium" == Medium == 500, which m3you already matches — and it violates no CLAUDE.md rule. Deleting the line is a pure no-op refactor, not an actionable defect.

Checkbox.summary: The Checkbox has no pressed state layer at all: there is no `:active` CSS rule, and the `<Ripple />` that would supply it is mounted inside `.md-checkbox__state-layer`, which sets `pointer-events: none`, so m3-ripple's capture listeners (attached to `ripple.parentElement`) never receive a pointer event.
Checkbox.ours: `` (checkbox.tsx:61-63) with `pointer-events: none` on that span (checkbox.css:27); no `:active` / pressed background-color rule anywhere in checkbox.css
Checkbox.kit: Every `State=Pressed` variant has state-layer fill at 0.12 opacity — #1c1b1f@0.12 (On Surface) for Unselected, #6750a4@0.12 (Primary) for Selected/Indeterminate, #b3261e@0.12 (Error) for the Error types
Checkbox.fix: Mount `<Ripple />` in its own `pointer-events: auto`-eligible wrapper (as RadioButton does at radio-button.tsx:73, though it has the same bug) or add an explicit `.md-checkbox:active .md-checkbox__state-layer` rule at --md-sys-state-pressed-opacity, and set `--ripple-color` to the correct role

verdicts.reason: Reproduced both sides. Kit: every State=Pressed variant has a state-layer fill at 0.12 — Unselected #1c1b1f@0.12, Selected/Indeterminate #6750a4@0.12 (= Schemes/Primary), Error* #b3261e@0.12 (= Schemes/Error); I dumped the raw fills for all six Types. m3you: I read all 118 lines of checkbox.css — there is no `:active` selector and no pressed background-color rule anywhere; only :hover (38-44) and :has(input:focus-visible) (46-52). The ripple mechanism claim also checks out: checkbox.tsx:61-63 mounts <Ripple/> inside `.md-checkbox__state-layer`, and node_modules/m3-ripple/dist/index.js:54-57 attaches its listeners to `ripple.current.parentElement` with capture=true. checkbox.css:27 sets `pointer-events: none` on that span, so it is never a hit-test target and is never in the event path (it is a descendant of the label, not an ancestor, so capture does not reach it either) — the capture listeners never fire. No other stylesheet touches md-checkbox (grepped src/). Pressed state is genuinely absent.

Mechanism independently confirmed in the ripple source. node_modules/m3-ripple/dist/index.js attaches all pointer listeners to `u.current.parentElement` (the element containing the .salty-ripple div) with capture=true. In Checkbox that parent is `.md-checkbox__state-layer` (checkbox.tsx:61-63), which has `pointer-events: none` (checkbox.css:27), so it can never be the hit-test target; and because it is a SIBLING of the box/input rather than an ancestor, it is never on the capture or bubble path of events targeting the label — the listeners can never fire. Ripple's own CSS also sets `.salty-ripple { pointer-events: none }`, so nothing rescues it. checkbox.css contains no `:active` rule (full file read, 119 lines) and no other stylesheet defines `.md-checkbox` rules, so there is zero pressed feedback. Kit side confirmed: every State=Pressed variant has a state-layer fill at 0.12 — #1c1b1f@0.12 (Unselected), #6750a4@0.12 = Primary (Selected/Indeterminate), #b3261e@0.12 = Error (all three Error types); --md-sys-state-pressed-opacity: 0.12 already exists at sys.state.css:9. Downgrading to medium: hover and focus layers do render, so this is a missing interaction state rather than a wrong default rendering.

ExtendableFab.kitVariant: n/a — Buttons / Extended FAB State axis is [Pressed|Focused|Hovered|Enabled] only; precedent is src/components/Button/button.css:47-56
ExtendableFab.fix: Replace the blanket opacity with explicit disabled container/label colors mirroring button.css:47-56, keeping box-shadow: none.

verdicts.reason: m3you side confirmed: extendable-fab.css:62-67 applies `opacity: var(--md-sys-state-disabled-opacity)` = 0.38 (sys.state.css:11) to the whole button. The kit facts are right — Buttons/Extended FAB and Buttons/FAB both expose Color=[Tertiary|Secondary|Primary|Tertiary container|Secondary container|Primary container] — but this is an API-surface expansion request, not a defect in the rendered component. Dialog.summary: The dialog has no max-height and no scrolling body, so tall content overflows a position:fixed centered box while page scroll is locked, making the footer actions unreachable.
Dialog.ours: .md-dialog-content sets display:grid, position:fixed, top:50%/left:50% with translate(-50%,-50%), but declares no max-height; .md-dialog-body (line 80) has no overflow or min-height.
Dialog.kit: Dialogs / Scrollable list dialog, Icon=False: Content > 'List container' [312x170] clips a 'List (baseline)' [312x683] child, i.e. a fixed-height scrolling body between a pinned Title & Description and a pinned Actions row.
Dialog.fix: Add max-height: calc(100% - 48px) and grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto to .md-dialog-content, and overflow-y: auto on .md-dialog-body.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced both sides. Kit `Dialogs / Scrollable list dialog` Icon=False: variant [312x434] > Content [312x346] > 'List container' [312x170] wrapping a 'List (baseline)' [312x683] child — the container is 513px shorter than its content, i.e. a clipped/scrolling region pinned between 'text content' (pad=24,24,24,24) and 'Actions' (pad=20,24,20,16). m3you dialog.css:23-45 `.md-dialog-content` declares position:fixed; top:50%; left:50%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); display:grid and NO max-height; lines 79-88 `.md-dialog-description, .md-dialog-body` set only typography (no overflow, no min-height). I grepped all of src/ — `md-dialog-content` appears only at dialog.css:23 and dialog.tsx:72, and @base-ui/react 1.6.0 DialogPopup.js sets no inline maxHeight — so nothing else caps the height. Because the popup is position:fixed, overflow is unreachable regardless of scroll lock, so the footer/actions become unclickable. The fullscreen variant does handle this (dialog.css:156-160 sets flex:1 + overflow-y:auto), which makes the omission on the standard dialog a clear gap.

Reproduced both sides. m3you: computed max-height on .md-dialog-content is 'none' and .md-dialog-body overflow-y is 'visible' (src/components/Dialog/dialog.css:23-42, :80-89). Rendered a 30-row body at a 1200x800 viewport: content box is 1380.8px tall, top=-290.4 (title clipped above the viewport) and the .md-dialog-footer rect sits at y=1045.4-1066.4, i.e. entirely below the fold, with document.documentElement.scrollHeight=800. Because the popup is position:fixed, page scroll can never bring it back regardless of Base UI's modal scroll lock, so the actions are genuinely unreachable. Kit: Dialogs/Scrollable list dialog Icon=False has 'List container' [312x170] wrapping a 'List (baseline)' [312x683] child between a padded 'text content' block and a pinned 'Actions' [312x88] row - a clipped, fixed-height scrolling region. Note .design-sync/measurements.json contains no md-dialog-content element (all dialog stories captured closed), so the oracle neither confirms nor refutes; I measured it directly. One caveat on the proposed fix: the hardcoded grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto is fragile - the rendered grid currently has 5 implicit rows (71.81px 70px 64px 18px 45px) because header/description/body/divider/footer are all optional; max-height plus min-height:0 and overflow-y:auto on the body is the safe form.

Dialog.summary: md-dialog-divider only overrides border-color, leaving the UA stylesheet's border-style:inset and 1px border on all four sides, so it renders as a ~2px inset-shaded line with 8px block margins instead of a clean 1px rule.

Dialog.fix: Mirror .md-divider (divider.css:8-13): add border-width: 0; border-style: solid; border-top-width: 1px; margin-block: 0.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. dialog.tsx:141-143 renders DialogDivider as a bare `<hr>`; dialog.css:91-93 sets only `border-color: var(--md-sys-color-outline-variant)`. Nothing resets `hr` anywhere in src/ (grepped globals.css, utilities.css, all component CSS — zero hr rules), so Chrome's UA rule `hr { border-style: inset; border-width: 1px; margin-block: 0.5em; overflow: hidden }` survives: a 2px-tall two-tone inset line with ~8px block margins (font-size is inherited at 16px; .md-dialog-content sets none). Kit `Dialogs / Basic dialog` Icon=False contains `Horizontal/Full-width <INSTANCE> [312x1]` — a 1px rule. The sibling .md-divider (divider.css:6-13) does the correct reset (border-width:0; border-style:solid; border-top-width:1px), confirming the intended pattern. Stories/Dialog.stories.tsx:242 and :272 already patch around it with inline marginBottom/marginTop, which only overrides one side and leaves the UA 0.5em on the other.

Reproduced both sides, and the real behaviour is worse than described. dialog.css:91-93 sets only border-color, so Chrome's UA rule (hr { border-style:inset; border-width:1px; margin-block:0.5em; margin-inline:auto; overflow:hidden }) survives intact. The repo's own Showcase story does exactly this at stories/Dialog.stories.tsx:596 and :600 (DialogDivider as a direct child of DialogContent, outside DialogBody), so a shipped story renders two invisible 2x2 dots instead of two rules. The proposed fix (mirror src/components/Divider/divider.css:8-13) is correct but incomplete: md-divider itself measures 0x1 as a grid child for the same auto-margin reason, so margin-inline:0 (not just margin-block:0) is required.
verdicts.correction: Not merely 'a ~2px inset line with 8px margins'. Two distinct failures: (a) inside DialogBody it is 512x2 with 1px inset borders on all four sides and 7px block margins; (b) as a direct grid child of .md-dialog-content it collapses to a 2x2px box centred by the UA's margin-inline:auto, i.e. the divider disappears entirely - which is how stories/Dialog.stories.tsx:596 and :600 use it. The fix must reset margin-inline as well as margin-block.

Dialog.kit: Dialogs / List dialog, Icon=False: 'Title & Description' has pad=24,24,24,24 but the sibling 'List (baseline)' is [312x170] — the full 312 container width with zero inset; likewise the Basic dialog divider is [312x1].
Dialog.fix: Move the 24px inset off the container onto .md-dialog-header/.md-dialog-description/.md-dialog-footer (keep 24px block padding on the container), so DialogBody children can run full-bleed.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced both sides. Kit `Dialogs / List dialog` Icon=False: Content [312x346] has pad=[0,0,0,0]; only its 'Title & Description' child carries pad=24,24,24,24, while the sibling 'List (baseline)' is [312x170] — the full container width, zero inset. Same shape in Scrollable list dialog ('List container' [312x170] full-bleed) and Basic dialog ('Horizontal/Full-width' [312x1] full-bleed). m3you dialog.css:35 puts `padding: 24px` on .md-dialog-content, so every DialogBody child is inset 24px per side: a divider inside DialogBody renders 264 wide against the kit's 312 at the same container width (48px short). This is exercised in practice — stories/Dialog.stories.tsx:220-273 (WithDividerAndList) puts DialogDivider and an account list inside DialogBody.

Both raw numbers check out (kit List dialog Icon=False: 'Title & Description' pad=24,24,24,24 vs 'List (baseline)' [312x170] at full container width; m3you .md-dialog-body renders at x=24 w=342 inside a 390px box), but the conclusion does not survive. (a) 'Impossible' is false - DialogBody is a plain div that forwards className/style (dialog.tsx:129-131), so margin-inline:-24px gives full bleed today. (b) No m3you element is measurably wrong against any kit variant: I checked the Basic dialog and it matches exactly - kit Title&Description pad=24,24,0,24 vs m3you container padding 24; kit gap 16 vs .md-dialog-description margin-top 16; kit Actions pad=20,24,20,8 around 48dp touch targets holding 40px visible buttons = 24px to the visible button on all sides, vs m3you footer margin-top 24 + container padding-bottom 24 with 40px buttons (height 40 confirmed in measurements.json). (c) The proposed fix regresses that match: stripping inline padding from the container and putting it only on header/description/footer leaves every plain-text DialogBody flush against the 28px-radius edge - and none of the repo's dialog stories composes a kit-style list anyway (they use inline-styled divs, e.g. stories/Dialog.stories.tsx:837-944). This is an API ergonomics preference, not a fidelity defect.

Dialog.summary: The dialog paints an elevation-3 drop shadow, but the Expressive kit gives scrimmed modal surfaces no shadow at all.
Dialog.kit: No `effects` node anywhere in the three Dialogs sets. The same kit file proves this is deliberate rather than an omission: Sheets / Bottom sheet Modal=False carries shadow=DROP_SHADOW r3 y1 #0000004d;DROP_SHADOW r8 y4 #00000026, while Modal=True (scrimmed) carries none.
Dialog.fix: Drop the box-shadow from .md-dialog-content and let the surface-container-high tonal step carry the separation.
Dialog.kitVariant: Dialogs / Basic dialog — Icon=False vs Sheets / Bottom sheet — Modal=True/False

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. m3you dialog.css:36 is `box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-3)` (= 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0 4px 8px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.15) per sys.elevation.css:10). Kit side: `grep -o DROP_SHADOW Dialogs__*.json` returns 0 across all three dialog sets, and the raw JSON has no `effects` key anywhere in them. The control the finding cites checks out exactly: `Sheets / Bottom sheet` Modal=False carries shadow=DROP_SHADOW r3 y1 #0000004d;DROP_SHADOW r8 y4 #00000026 while Modal=True (which carries a Scrim instance at [492x794] opacity=0.32) carries none. Additional corroboration I found: Modal date picker has 0 shadows too, while Menu (12), Snackbar (20) and FAB (8) all do record shadows — so the kit does encode elevation, it just withholds it from scrimmed surfaces. Caveat worth flagging to the fixer: this is one of the few places the kit contradicts the published m3.material.io dialog spec (which states Level 3), so it is a kit-vs-docs judgement call, not an unambiguous bug.

The m3you side is real (computed box-shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.3) 0 1px 3px, rgba(0,0,0,0.15) 0 4px 8px 3px = --md-sys-elevation-3) and the kit side is literally true (0 occurrences of "effects" in all three Dialogs__*.json), but the inference is unsound because this kit's shadow data is demonstrably not a systematic elevation encoding. Same-file counterexample: Menu__Menu.json carries [r3 sp0 off0,1 #0000004d; r8 sp3 off0,4 #00000026] = elevation level 3, while Menu__Menu-baseline.json carries [r6 sp2 off0,2 #00000026; r2 sp0 off0,1 #0000004d] = level 2 - the same conceptual component with two different elevations. The identical level-3 pair is also copy-pasted onto Snackbar (spec level 3), Bottom sheet Modal=False (spec level 1, and m3you deliberately uses elevation-1 at bottom-sheet.css:42) and Button-elevated (spec level 1). The finding's own control is therefore contaminated: the Modal=False sheet's shadow is a level-3 value on a level-1 surface. Also, unlike Sheets/Bottom sheet Modal=True, the Dialogs frames contain no Scrim child at all, so the 'scrimmed surfaces get no shadow' narrative is not what the file shows. Absence of an effects node here is an authoring artifact, not authority to drop the spec-mandated dialog elevation.

Verified there is no defect. Divider.summary: `.md-divider` never resets the UA `hr { margin-inline: auto }`, so a Divider placed in any flex-column container collapses to 0 inline size and disappears — this is a component robustness bug, not a story-layout artifact.
Divider.ours: No margin declaration at all on `.md-divider`; the Chromium UA sheet's `margin-inline-start/end: auto` survives. Per CSS Flexbox, `stretch` does not apply to a flex item with an auto cross-axis margin, so the empty `hr` is sized to fit-content = 0. measurements.json `containment-divider--variants`: full-width w=0 h=1, heavy w=0 h=8, while `inset` in the *same* 320px flex-column parent measures w=288 — the only difference being that `inset` overrides margin-inline. Same file, same story, controlled A/B.
Divider.kit: A divider is a 1dp line flush to the full inline size of its container with no intrinsic margin: Lists/List "Divider 01" [280x1], Tabs/Tabs "Divider" [360x1], Sheets/Side Sheet "Horizontal divider" [320x1], Lists/List item 0-Density "Divider" [360x1].
Divider.fix: Add `margin: 0;` to the `.md-divider` base rule at divider.css:6 (the `inset` variant's `margin-inline: 16px` at line 22 still wins by source order), matching sibling `.md-list-divider` (src/components/List/list.css:287) and `.md-menu-divider` (src/components/Menu/menu.css:159) which both already zero the UA margin.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced both sides. Kit: /tmp/figspec/Lists__List.json "Divider 01" size=[280,1] pad=[0,16,0,16]; Tabs__Tabs.json "Divider" [360,1] pad=[0,0,0,0]; Sheets__Side-Sheet.json "Horizontal divider" [320,1] pad=[0,0,0,0]; Lists__List-item-List-Item-0-Density-baseline.json "Divider" [360,1] pad=[0,0,0,0] — every kit divider spans the full inline size of its container with no intrinsic margin. m3you: /home/dev/bczak/m3you/src/components/Divider/divider.css:6-10 declares flex-shrink/border-width/border-style/border-color and NO margin; I grepped src/styles/globals.css, src/styles/** and every component .css and found zero `hr` or global margin reset, so Blink's UA `hr { margin-inline-start/end: auto; color: gray }` survives. Confirmed the body never scrolls: #bd scrollHeight 2024 === clientHeight 2024, overflows=false, so the `flex:1; overflow-y:auto` at bottom-sheet.css:66-68 is dead. Confirmed base-ui does not supply the bound: DrawerPopup.mjs only writes CSS vars (--drawer-popup-height, --drawer-snap-point-offset) via style, never height/max-height, and DrawerPopup.mjs:184 `measureHeight` reads popupElement.offsetHeight, so snap points are computed FROM the unbounded popup. Verified the proposed fix works: max-height: calc(100% - 72px) → top 72, height 421, body overflows true. Kit side confirms a bound is intended (Bottom Sheet 412x480 inside a 492x794 Scrim). Real functional bug.
verdicts.correction: Exact numbers with the real DOM (48px drag-handle header + 24px body padding-bottom) are height 2072 / top -1579 at a 412x493 viewport; the reported 2000/-1507 corresponds to the bare-content control. Substance unchanged.

BottomSheet.summary: At viewports >=640px `margin-inline: 56px` over-constrains the absolutely-positioned popup, so `right` is dropped and the sheet is pinned 56px from the left edge instead of being centred.
BottomSheet.ours: @media (min-width: 640px) { margin-inline: 56px } combined with left:0/right:0/max-width:640px — verified in Chromium at a 780px viewport: left=56, right=696 (centred would be 70/710); at 1440px it lands at left=56 instead of left=400
BottomSheet.kit: Bottom Sheet spans the full 412 width of the 412-wide screen frame, i.e. horizontally symmetric
BottomSheet.kitVariant: Sheets / Bottom sheet — Modal=True / Modal=False (Bottom Sheet [412x480] in a 412-wide screen)
BottomSheet.fix: Keep `margin-inline: auto` and cap the width instead, e.g. `max-width: min(640px, 100% - 112px)` in the media query.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly in headless Chromium. At viewport 780x800: .md-bottom-sheet-content resolves to left=56, right edge=696, width=640, computed margin-left/right=56px, computed right stays '0px' but is over-constrained and dropped (left gap 56 vs right gap 84; centred would be 70/710). At viewport 1440x900: left=56, right edge=696, width=640 -- centred would be left=400, so it is 344px off-centre. Cause confirmed at bottom-sheet.css:32-38,45-48: left:0 + right:0 + margin-inline:56px + max-width:640px means width auto resolves to cbw-112, gets clamped to 640 above a 752px viewport, and CSS then ignores `right` in ltr. Kit side: Sheets/Bottom sheet Modal=True/False both have Bottom Sheet [412x480] filling the full 412-wide screen frame, i.e. horizontally symmetric -- nothing in the kit supports a left-pinned sheet.

Reproduced in Chromium across viewport widths with left:0/right:0/max-width:640px/margin-inline:56px (bottom-sheet.css:32-36,45-48). 412px: left 0, w 412. 700px: left 56, right 644, w 588 — centred (cbW-112 < 640, width solves normally). 760px: left 56, right 696, w 640 (centred would be left 60). 780px: left 56, right 696, w 640 (centred = left 70) — exactly the finding's numbers. 1000px: left 56 (centred = 180). 1440px: left 56 (centred = 400). Mechanism confirmed: once max-width:640px clamps the solved width, left/right/width/margins are all non-auto, so per §10.3.7 `right` is ignored in LTR and the box pins to left+56. computedStyle still reports right '0px', which is why it looks correct in source. The breakpoint where it goes wrong is viewport >= 752px, not 640px — below that the 56px inline margins are genuinely symmetric, which is clearly the authored intent, so this is an unintended resolution, not a deliberate choice.
verdicts.correction: The asymmetry only begins at viewport width >= 752px (640 + 2*56); between 640px and 752px the sheet is still symmetric at 56/56. At 780px it is left 56 / right 696 (centred would be 70/710); at 1440px left 56 instead of 400.

BottomSheet.ours: box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-1) = 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0px 1px 3px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.15) — applied to modal and standard alike
BottomSheet.kit: Modal=False: DROP_SHADOW r3 y1 sp0 #0000004d + DROP_SHADOW r8 y4 sp3 #00000026 (byte-for-byte --md-sys-elevation-3). Modal=True: no `effects` on the Bottom Sheet frame
BottomSheet.kitVariant: Sheets / Bottom sheet — Modal=False (effects array) vs Modal=True (no effects)
BottomSheet.fix: Use `box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-3)` for the standard sheet and `var(--md-sys-elevation-0)` when a scrim is present.

Modal=False > Bottom Sheet has effects [{DROP_SHADOW r:3 sp:0 off:[0,1] c:#0000004d}, {DROP_SHADOW r:8 sp:3 off:[0,4] c:#00000026}] which is 0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0px 4px 8px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.15) == --md-sys-elevation-3 exactly (src/styles/tokens/sys.elevation.css:10). Modal=True > Bottom Sheet has no `effects` key at all. m3you side reproduced at bottom-sheet.css:42: box-shadow: var(--md-sys-elevation-1) = 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0px 1px 3px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.15) (sys.elevation.css:8), applied unconditionally because nothing in the CSS or the component distinguishes modal from standard. Both the level (1 vs 3) and the modal case (shadow vs none) are wrong.

Verified byte-for-byte from the kit raw JSON. Modal=False → Bottom Sheet frame effects: [{DROP_SHADOW, r:3, sp:0, off:[0,1], c:'#0000004d'}, {DROP_SHADOW, r:8, sp:3, off:[0,4], c:'#00000026'}] = 0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0px 4px 8px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.15), which is exactly src/styles/tokens/sys.elevation.css:10 --md-sys-elevation-3. Modal=True's Bottom Sheet frame has no `effects` key at all. m3you bottom-sheet.css:42 applies var(--md-sys-elevation-1) = 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0px 1px 3px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.15) unconditionally. The 'level 3 for the standard sheet' half is exact; the 'level 0 for modal' half is the literal kit reading (a Figma author dropping an invisible shadow behind a scrim is plausible), so I'd treat that half as lower-confidence.
verdicts.correction: The standard (Modal=False) → elevation-3 half is exact and byte-verified. The 'modal → elevation-0' half rests on the absence of an `effects` key on the Modal=True frame, which may be Figma authoring convenience rather than a spec statement; fix the standard case with confidence, treat the modal case as optional.

BottomSheet.kitVariant: Sheets / Bottom sheet — Modal=True, Bottom Sheet > Header

verdicts.reason: Kit side reproduced: Sheets/Bottom sheet, both variants, Bottom Sheet > Header is FRAME [412x36] layout pad [16,16,16,16] gap 12 wrapping the single [32x4] Drag handle -- 16+4+16 = 36, and the frame's own recorded height is 36. m3you side reproduced by measurement, not just by reading the declaration: in headless Chromium .md-bottom-sheet-drag-handle renders 48px tall with computed padding '22px 0px' around a 4px indicator (bottom-sheet.css:52-56), so 22+4+22 = 48. Not a rule-1 touch-target artefact: the kit Header is the visible header layout frame (the only touch-target-sized frame in this set is the 412x480 variant), and m3you's handle wrapper is a plain non-interactive div (bottom-sheet.tsx:86-88), so there is no touch-target justification for the extra 12px. Everything below the handle is pushed down 12px.

Both sides reproduced. Kit: Header frame is [412x36] with layout.pad [16,16,16,16] hugging the single 4px Drag handle child — 16+4+16 = 36, and Content starts at y=36 (Content frame 412x444, 36+444 = 480 = sheet height, so the header really is 36 in the kit's own arithmetic). m3you: measured the real rule (padding-block:22px, bottom-sheet.css:55) in Chromium — .dh getBoundingClientRect().height = 48. So content starts 12px lower than the kit. Downgrading to low: 22px is (48-4)/2, i.e. a deliberate 48dp touch target for the grab affordance (matching Android's BottomSheetDragHandleView), which is a defensible a11y choice even though it is undocumented in the file — the header comment at bottom-sheet.css:1-6 says nothing about it. verdicts.correction: Severity low, not medium — the 48px is almost certainly an intentional 48dp touch target ((48-4)/2 = 22), just undocumented; the fix is a real fidelity gain but costs the grab-target size.

BottomSheet.summary: The kit's only variant axis (Modal) is not exposed on the popup element, so CSS cannot style the modal vs standard difference the kit specifies.
BottomSheet.ours: `<DrawerPrimitive.Popup data-slot="bottom-sheet-content" className={cx('md-bottom-sheet-content', className)}>` — `isModal` is read at line 74 only to decide whether to render the Backdrop; it is never forwarded as a data attribute
BottomSheet.kit: Bottom sheet set has exactly one axis: Modal=[True|False], and the two variants differ visually (shadow present only on Modal=False)
BottomSheet.fix: Add `data-modal={isModal ? 'true' : 'false'}` to the Popup and drive the elevation from it, mirroring how SideSheet uses `data-variant="standard"|"modal"`.

verdicts.reason: Kit side reproduced: the set has exactly one axis, Modal=[True|False], and the two variants genuinely differ (Modal=False carries the two DROP_SHADOWs, Modal=True carries none and adds the Scrim). m3you side reproduced: bottom-sheet.tsx:74 reads isModal from context and uses it only at line 78 to conditionally render the Backdrop; the Popup at lines 80-84 receives only data-slot="bottom-sheet-content" and the class, so no selector can distinguish the two states (the backdrop is a preceding sibling of the viewport, so not reachable from the popup in CSS either). This is really the enabling gap for finding 3 rather than an independent visual defect, hence low.

No independent defect. The kit's Modal axis has exactly two visual consequences: the Scrim child (present only on Modal=True) and the drop shadow (present only on Modal=False). m3you already implements the first — bottom-sheet.tsx:22 `const isModal = modal !== false` and :78 conditionally renders DrawerPrimitive.Backdrop. The second is finding [3]. So [5] is not a defect on its own; it is the implementation mechanism for [3]'s fix, and reporting it separately double-counts the same gap. I did confirm the SideSheet precedent the finding cites is factually accurate (side-sheet.tsx:83 `data-variant={variant}`, side-sheet.css:39/43 `&[data-variant="standard"|"modal"]`), but a missing data attribute that no CSS currently consumes renders identically to the current code — nothing to observe, nothing that breaks.

BottomSheet.summary: All BottomSheet motion CSS (swipe transform, enter/exit translateY(100%), transition) lives in the global stylesheet instead of the co-located component stylesheet, against CLAUDE.md's co-location rule.
BottomSheet.ours: `[data-slot="bottom-sheet-content"] { transform: translateY(calc(var(--drawer-snap-point-offset,0px) + var(--drawer-swipe-movement-y,0px))); transition: ... }` at src/styles/globals.css:273-285, while src/components/BottomSheet/bottom-sheet.css contains no transform or transition for the popup
BottomSheet.kit: n/a — repo rule: "CSS co-located as {name}.css in the component directory"
BottomSheet.fix: Move the three `[data-slot="bottom-sheet-content"]` blocks into src/components/BottomSheet/bottom-sheet.css (as `.md-bottom-sheet-content` rules) so the component's motion is discoverable next to its geometry.

verdicts.reason: The facts check out but this is not a defect. src/styles/globals.css:273-285 does hold the three [data-slot="bottom-sheet-content"] transform/transition blocks and bottom-sheet.css has no popup transform, but that section of globals.css is an established repo-wide home for exactly this kind of rule: SideSheet's five identical drawer-transform blocks sit immediately below at lines 287-313, and ConnectedButtonGroup (98-155), MenuGroup (157-188) and MenuGrouped (190-212) structural CSS live in the same file. CLAUDE.md describes the component directory pattern; it does not ban globals.css component rules, and the finding itself lists the kit side as 'n/a' with 'read from: unstated' -- there is no measurable defect on either side. With cssCodeSplit:false every one of these files is concatenated into the same dist/styles/globals.css, so moving the block changes zero bytes of rendered output. Singling out BottomSheet for a convention four other components share is noise in a design-kit audit.

No kit side exists — the finding's own `kit:` field says 'n/a', so nothing was reproduced against the Design Kit, which is what this audit is scoped to. On the repo-rule side it is also weak: globals.css:270-313 is a deliberate, commented, cross-component section ('Bottom Sheet — CSS variable-based transforms for Base UI Drawer' at :271, 'Side Sheet — ...' at :289) that holds the SAME kind of rules for both drawer-based components, so it is a consistent authored decision rather than a slip. I checked for a functional consequence and there is none: `[data-slot="bottom-sheet-content"]` (0,1,0) and `.md-bottom-sheet-content` (0,1,0) have equal specificity but declare disjoint properties (transform/transition vs box model, colour, radius), and base-ui writes/removes `transform` and `transition` as inline styles anyway (DrawerViewport.mjs:326, :382), which outrank both. Moving the block would be a pure reshuffle with zero rendered change.

BottomSheet.summary: `modal="trap-focus"` renders the 32% scrim, contradicting the story and the kit's Modal=False presentation which has no scrim.
BottomSheet.ours: bottom-sheet.tsx:22 `const isModal = modal !== false` => trap-focus renders `.md-bottom-sheet-backdrop` (asserted by tests/bottom-sheet.test.tsx:125-135), yet the story copy reads "Behaves like a standard sheet (no scrim)"
BottomSheet.kit: Modal=True is the only variant with a Scrim child; Modal=False has none
BottomSheet.kitVariant: Sheets / Bottom sheet — Modal=True (Scrim [492x794] fill=Schemes/Scrim opacity=0.32) vs Modal=False (no Scrim)
BottomSheet.fix: Either render the backdrop only for `modal === true` (so trap-focus matches the kit's Modal=False look) or correct the story/JSDoc copy to state that trap-focus keeps the scrim.

verdicts.reason: Both sides reproduced. Kit: Modal=True has the Scrim INSTANCE [492x794] fill=Schemes/Scrim opacity=0.32; Modal=False has no Scrim child. m3you: bottom-sheet.tsx:22 `const isModal = modal !== false`, so 'trap-focus' takes the isModal branch at line 78 and renders .md-bottom-sheet-backdrop (32% scrim, bottom-sheet.css:9-14); tests/bottom-sheet.test.tsx:125-135 asserts that as intended behaviour ('modal="trap-focus" still renders a backdrop'). The contradiction is in the documentation: stories/BottomSheet.stories.tsx:161 and :170 state 'no scrim' / 'Behaves like a standard sheet (no scrim)' for the trap-focus story, and the prop JSDoc at bottom-sheet.tsx:13-15 frames modal as 'modal (with scrim) or standard (no scrim)'. Real and actionable, but it is a doc-vs-behaviour bug rather than a kit measurement defect (the kit has no third state to arbitrate what trap-focus should look like), so low.

Reproduced the contradiction on both sides. Story: stories/BottomSheet.stories.tsx:161 section comment "modal: 'trap-focus' — no scrim, but keyboard focus stays trapped" and :170 body copy "Behaves like a standard sheet (no scrim) but traps keyboard focus inside while open", on a story that renders `<BottomSheet modal="trap-focus">` at :164. Behaviour: bottom-sheet.tsx:22 `const isModal = modal !== false` is true for 'trap-focus', so :78 renders the Backdrop, and bottom-sheet.css:13 paints it at color-mix(... scrim 32% ...). I checked base-ui in case it suppresses the backdrop for trap-focus: DrawerBackdrop.mjs sets only `pointerEvents: !open ? 'none' : undefined` and never reads `modal` (the only trap-focus branch in the package is useDialogRoot.mjs:51, which changes outside-press sensitivity, not backdrop rendering) — so the 32% scrim is fully visible AND pointer-capturing while open. tests/bottom-sheet.test.tsx:125-135 ('modal="trap-focus" still renders a backdrop') locks the behaviour in, so the code is intentional and the doc copy is the wrong half. Low severity: a docs/behaviour mismatch, not a kit deviation (the kit has no trap-focus variant).
verdicts.correction: This is a documentation defect, not a kit mismatch — the kit has no trap-focus variant to compare against. The actionable fix is correcting stories/BottomSheet.stories.tsx:161,170 (and clarifying the JSDoc at bottom-sheet.tsx:13-16) to say trap-focus keeps the scrim; changing the rendering would contradict the intentional test at tests/bottom-sheet.test.tsx:125.

Chip.summary: The hover state layer is dead CSS: color-mix() is given a unitless 0.08 where a <percentage> is required, so the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the background stays transparent.
Chip.ours: background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--md-sys-color-on-surface) var(--md-sys-state-hover-opacity), transparent) — Chromium computes rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); same bug at chip.css:201-205 for .md-chip__close:hover
Chip.kit: state-layer fill = #49454f (Schemes/On Surface Variant) at 8% on Hovered, e.g. "Style=Outlined, Configuration=Label & icon, State=Hovered"
Chip.fix: background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant) calc(var(--md-sys-state-hover-opacity) * 100%), transparent) — the pattern already used correctly at src/components/List/list.css:308
Chip.kitVariant: Chips / Assistive chip — Style=Outlined, Configuration=Label & icon, State=Hovered

verdicts.reason: Reproduced empirically. I launched Chromium via the repo's own playwright and evaluated three divs: `color-mix(in srgb, rgb(67,71,79) var(--o), transparent)` with `--o:0.08` computes to `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`; the literal `color-mix(in srgb, rgb(67,71,79) 0.08, transparent)` also computes to `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`; only `calc(var(--o)*100%)` computes to `color(srgb 0.262745 0.278431 0.309804 / 0.08)`. src/styles/tokens/sys.state.css:8 defines `--md-sys-state-hover-opacity: 0.08` (unitless), and chip.css:66-71 feeds it straight into color-mix, as does chip.css:201-205 with `--md-sys-state-pressed-opacity: 0.12`. Since the outlined chip's rest background is `transparent` (chip.css:61), the hover produces zero visual change. Kit side also reproduces: Chips/Assistive chip, Style=Outlined, Configuration=Label only, State=Hovered has state-layer fill `#49454f` opacity 0.08, and `node q.js --var 'on surface'` shows M3/Schemes/On Surface Variant = #49454f. So the role should be on-surface-variant, not on-surface. Both halves confirmed.

Reproduced in Chromium (playwright from .design-sync/node_modules): `background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--md-sys-color-on-surface) var(--md-sys-state-hover-opacity), transparent)` with --md-sys-state-hover-opacity:0.08 (sys.state.css:7) computes to rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); the calc(...*100%) form computes to color(srgb 0.101961 0.109804 0.121569 / 0.08). It is invalid-at-computed-value-time, so background-color falls back to its initial value (transparent), not to the earlier `background-color: transparent` — either way, zero hover feedback on the DEFAULT outlined variant and on .md-chip__close (chip.css:201-205 uses pressed-opacity the same way). Kit side confirmed: Chips/Assistive chip Style=Outlined, Configuration=Label & icon, State=Hovered -> state-layer fill=#49454f@0.08, and #49454f is M3/Schemes/On Surface Variant per --var. The same unitless bug exists at Switch/switch.css:49,53,57, Checkbox/checkbox.css:39-51, RadioButton/radio-button.css:47-55, ExtendableFab/extendable-fab.css:179 — only List/list.css:308 uses the correct calc pattern.
verdicts.correction: Two defects in one: the value is invalid (dead CSS) AND the role is wrong (kit uses On Surface Variant @8%, not On Surface). The proposed fix already corrects both.

Chip.summary: Closable input chips render 34px tall instead of 32px because the .md-chip--closable root is a <span> (content-box) rather than a <button> (UA border-box), so the 1px border is added outside the declared 32px height.
Chip.ours: 34px tall — measurements.json selection-chip--removable-input / --input-group / --with-avatar all report height 34 with borderRadius 8px, while every non-closable chip reports 32
Chip.kit: Container 32x32-high in every Input chip variant, e.g. [81x32] with strokeAlign INSIDE
Chip.fix: add box-sizing: border-box to .md-chip (or at least to .md-chip--closable) so the 1px outline is drawn inside the 32px box
Chip.kitVariant: Chips / Input chip — Configuration=Label only, State=Enabled, Selected=False, Show closing icon=true

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. measurements.json: every `md-chip` in selection-chip--removable-input (3 elements), selection-chip--input-group (5) and selection-chip--with-avatar (4) reports height 34; the two closable entries inside selection-chip--input and selection-chip--all also report 34, while all 40+ non-closable chips report exactly 32. Cause confirmed: chip.tsx:126 renders a `<span class="md-chip md-chip--closable">` for the closable path, chip.css:10 sets `height: 32px` and chip.css:63 adds `border: 1px solid ...`, and there is no box-sizing declaration anywhere in src/styles (grep for box-sizing returns nothing) — so the span is content-box (32+1+1=34) while the `<button>` path gets Chromium's UA `box-sizing: border-box` (32 total). Kit: Chips/Input chip, Configuration=Label only, State=Enabled, Selected=False, Show closing icon=true is [81x32] with strokeWeight 1 / strokeAlign INSIDE, i.e. 32 including the stroke. Note this is a 2px delta, but it is visible as mismatched heights when closable and non-closable chips sit in the same row (the Input story does exactly that), so medium rather than high.

Confirmed on both sides and root-caused. measurements.json: every outlined closable chip is height 34 (selection-chip--removable-input x3, --input-group x5, --with-avatar x4, --input entries with close), while the elevated closable chip is 32 (no border) and every <button> chip is 32. Live Chromium check of the exact box: <span> with height:32px + 1px border -> box-sizing content-box, rect height 34; <button> with the identical rule -> Chrome UA gives box-sizing border-box, rect height 32 (and the UA 1px block padding explains the "1px 16px" in measurements). Kit: Chips/Input chip Configuration=Label only, State=Enabled, Selected=False, Show closing icon=true -> [81x32] with strokeAlign INSIDE, i.e. the 1dp stroke is inside the 32dp box. The proposed box-sizing:border-box fix is safe — the <button> root already resolves that way, so only the closable <span> changes.
verdicts.correction: Only the OUTLINED closable chip is 34; the elevated closable chip already measures 32 because it has no border. Practical impact is 32/34 misalignment when closable and non-closable chips share a row.

Assistive/Filter/Suggestion all do carry Style=[Elevated|Outlined]. m3you side reproduced: chip.tsx:13 declares `variant?: 'outlined' | 'elevated'` independent of `type`, and stories/Chip.stories.tsx:164-181 renders a full elevated input-chip column (five chips), which measurements.json selection-chip--input confirms as five elevated entries with background rgb(244,243,248). @material/web agrees with the kit here (md-input-chip has no `elevated` attribute while md-assist/filter/suggestion-chip do), so this is a genuine divergence rather than kit noise — though it is an unconstrained extension, not a wrong rendering of a kit-covered variant, so low is the right severity.

The kit observation is accurate — `q.js --list chip` shows Chips/Input chip axes = Configuration, State, Selected, Show closing icon, with no Style axis (the only Input-chip shadows are on the Dragged state). But this is not a defect against the kit: it is an API superset that m3you documents on purpose. chip.css:4 states "4 types (assist, filter, input, suggestion) x 2 variants (outlined, elevated)", and chip.tsx:11-13 declares `type` and `variant` as independent props by design. Offering an extra combination the kit does not enumerate produces no wrong pixels for any combination the kit DOES enumerate — nothing renders incorrectly, no token or role is misused. The proposed "fix" (narrowing the variant union by type) would be a breaking public-API change plus a conditional-type complication for a purely additive capability, so it fails the "would the fix break something else" test. At most this is a docs note, not an actionable defect.

Card Link
` and dumped Chrome's full AX tree via CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree — the inner button is exposed as role `button`, name `Inner`, ignored=false. Chrome does not apply presentational-children to focusable descendants, so "nested controls are lost to assistive tech" is false. There is a genuine authoring smell here (axe-core's nested-interactive rule fires on focusable descendants of an interactive role), but that is a different claim with a different consequence, and it is not a design-kit defect.

Kit side confirms cards host controls: Cards / Stacked card, Style=Elevated Layout=Media & text has `Icon button - standard [48x48]` in Header and `Secondary action [100x48]` + `Primary action [82x48]` in Actions. Carousel.summary: The item's hover/pressed state layer is painted underneath the item media, so carousel items have no visible state layer in any interactive state.
Carousel.ours: .md-carousel-item__action sets isolation:isolate (l.182) creating a stacking context; inside it <Ripple/> renders .salty-ripple with position:absolute and z-index:auto, while .md-carousel-item__content is position:relative; z-index:1 (carousel.css:201-202) and fills 100%x100% with the opaque media. Per CSS painting order the z-index:1 content paints above the z-index:auto ripple, so the 8% hover and 12% pressed layers are never visible.
Carousel.kit: M3 state layers must overlay the item surface; the repo's own tokens --md-sys-state-hover-opacity 0.08 / --md-sys-state-pressed-opacity 0.12 are meant to render on top of the container (cf. Card, which layers its ::before over the surface).
Carousel.fix: Give .salty-ripple inside .md-carousel-item__action a higher stacking level than the content (e.g. .md-carousel-item__action > .salty-ripple { z-index: 2 }) so the state layer overlays the media.

verdicts.reason: Verified by reading the actual painting order. carousel.css:182 puts `isolation: isolate` on `.md-carousel-item__action`; inside it CarouselItem renders `<Ripple/>` then `.md-carousel-item__content` (carousel.tsx:429-437). node_modules/m3-ripple/dist/ripple.css:1-11 gives `.salty-ripple` `position: absolute; inset: 0` with no z-index (auto), while carousel.css:200-202 gives the content `position: relative; z-index: 1` and 100%x100% sizing (carousel.css:204-205) with the media stretched to `object-fit: cover` (carousel.css:210-218). Per CSS 2.1 Appendix E, positioned z-index:auto descendants paint in step 6 and positive-z-index descendants in step 7, so the opaque media always paints over the 8%/12% ripple layers. Carousel has no ::before/::after state layer of its own (grep of carousel.css finds none), so there is no other hover/press affordance. Card avoids this only because its content is not opaque (card.css:25-36 uses the same z-index 0/1 split plus its own ::before layer).

Verified the whole stacking chain. .md-carousel-item__action sets isolation:isolate (carousel.css:182), and the Ripple is rendered first, before .md-carousel-item__content (carousel.tsx:431-432). node_modules/m3-ripple/dist/ripple.css:1-11 gives .salty-ripple position:absolute; inset:0 with NO z-index, and both state layers live inside it (.salty-ripple-surface::before at 8% for --hover, ::after at 12% for --press, lines 58-65). .md-carousel-item__content is position:relative; z-index:1 (carousel.css:200-202) at 100%x100% with scale(1.12), so by CSS painting order (positioned z-index:auto descendants paint in step 8, positive z-index in step 9) the content always paints over the ripple. Any opaque item media — the normal case for a carousel, and what every kit variant shows (fill=IMAGE on every item) — therefore hides the hover and pressed layers entirely. Card solves the same problem explicitly with `& > .salty-ripple { z-index: 0 }` plus its own ::before overlay (card.css:25-27, 12-22), which works there only because card content is not a full-bleed opaque surface.

Mechanism confirmed empirically in Chromium: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) var(--o), transparent)` with `--o: 0.08` computes to `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, and `CSS.supports('background-color','color-mix(in srgb, red 0.08, transparent)')` returns false while the `8%` form returns true. Only citation slip: the morph:false line is 43, not 44.

Kit numbers reproduced exactly in `Buttons/Building Blocks/Button group/Connected segments/{XSmall,Small,Medium,Large,Xlarge}`, Selected=False: Enabled r=4/8/8/16/20 → Hovered/Focused/Pressed r=12/12/16/28/32. m3you: button-group.css:184-205 sets --_connected-inner-radius statically to 4/8/8/16/20 (extra-small/small/small/large/large-increased), and the file contains no :hover, :focus-visible or :active radius rule at all. connected-button-group.tsx:42 passes `morph: false`, so Button's `[data-morph]…:active` radius rules (button.css:174-204) never match. verdicts.correction: The defect is real but the proposed fix as written would regress the group's outer corners: first/last segments carry compound radii (e.g. `calc(--_height/2) 4px 4px calc(--_height/2)`), and the kit keeps those outer corners fully round while hovered (End segment r=4/16/16/4 at XSmall, 8/28/28/8 at Medium). A blanket `border-radius: 12px` on hover would flatten the pill ends. The rule must raise only the INNER corners for :first-child/:last-child and all four only for middle segments.

verdicts.reason: Kit `Local M3 calendar cell Type=Selected, State=Hovered`: `container [40x40] r=100 fill=Schemes/Primary` with a nested `state-layer [40x40] fill=#ffffff@0.08`; State=Pressed is the same with @0.12. m3you date-picker.css:224 is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--md-sys-color-primary) 90%, transparent)` -> primary at 90% alpha, so the result depends on whatever is behind the grid rather than being a fixed On Primary overlay, and the opacity is 10% where the state token is 8%.
verdicts.correction: Direction right, rationale wrong: the kit's overlay is On Primary (white in light theme) at 8%, which also LIGHTENS the chip. The defect is that m3you drops the container to 90% alpha (backdrop-dependent compositing) instead of layering on-primary @ 0.08, and uses 10% where the kit/state token says 8% — not "lighter instead of darker".

verdicts.reason: Refuted on resolution. I computed both composites in Chromium with the real tokens. Light: ours = color(srgb 0.1529 0.3059 0.4980 / 0.9); over surface-container-high #e8e8ec that composites to (0.2286, 0.3663, 0.5408); the kit recipe color-mix(on-primary 8%, primary) = (0.2207, 0.3614, 0.5382). Delta = (2.0, 1.2, 0.7)/255 — invisible. Dark: ours composites to (0.6016, 0.7224, 0.9180) vs kit (0.5989, 0.7369, 0.9498); delta = (0.7, 3.7, 8.1)/255. The stated failure — 'the cell gets lighter/washed out rather than darker' — does not reproduce: on-primary is #ffffff in light theme, so the kit's own hover state layer lightens too, to within 2/255 of what m3you already produces. The only substantive difference is that the cell carries alpha 0.9 (would show a patterned/unknown consumer background through), which is a robustness nit, not the reported defect. The proposed fix would change essentially zero pixels.

Kit side: every Local M3 calendar cell 'Date' text node is [19x24] for the string '00' — 19px is exactly Roboto 16px digits (2 x 9.1 advance + 2 x 0.5 tracking) and the 24px height is lh24; Type=Prev/Next State=Hovered and State=Focused print '16px lh24px ls0.5 Roboto Regular' outright, which is M3 body-large verbatim (kit variable Typescale/Static/Body Large = Roboto Regular 16/24/0.5). The sibling .Building Blocks/Year cell is internally consistent at 16px lh24px [38x24]. Weight is Regular on Default/Today/Prev-Next and Medium only on Type=Selected, whereas m3you applies 500 to every day. So 14px/500 with no line-height and no tracking is wrong under any reading of the kit.

Proven empirically with the same oracle: `md-icon-button` is also a `<button>` (icon-button.tsx:50) with `--_height: 96px; height: var(--_height)` and `border: 2px solid` for outlined lg (icon-button.css:252-254), no `box-sizing` anywhere in icon-button.css, globals.css or .design-sync/preview-base.css — and measurements.json records width 96 / height 96 for it, captured via `getBoundingClientRect()` (scripts/measure-components.ts:127), i.e. the border box. Refuted — the cascade does not resolve that way. <button> carries box-sizing: border-box from the browser UA stylesheet (Blink/WebKit/Gecko all do this for form controls), so no repo reset is needed. I verified in headless Chromium: a bare <button style="width:40px;height:40px;border:1px solid red"> reports getComputedStyle().boxSizing === 'border-box' and getBoundingClientRect() 40x40. Rendering the real date-picker.css with a [data-state="today"] cell in the grid gives today = 40x40 at y=152, and every row top is exactly 40px apart (112, 152, 192, 232, 272, 312) — the today row is not 2px taller. The 42x42 / 2px-taller-row failure scenario does not occur. (This also means .design-sync/measurements.json's 328x356 root height is correct for a today-containing month too.)

DatePicker.fix: Track this as a deliberate scope decision or add a `mode="range"` axis plus optional header/actions slots; at minimum document that the consumer must supply the header and action row.

The claims check out factually (Modal date picker has Type=Full-screen (range) with a `header [360x132]` and `Local Actions [360x60] pad=4,12,8,12 gap=8`; Input date picker has Type=Range; the cell set has Type=Selected (Middle) with Range highlight start/middle/end filled Schemes/Secondary Container and text On Secondary Container), but this is a feature-scope statement about an API that deliberately ships as a bare calendar surface (date-picker.css:8-9: "No bg/shadow/radius — consumer provides the container"), and the finding's own remedy is "document it". There is no measurement in the implementation that disagrees with the kit.

Not a defect. The header/actions half is an explicitly documented delegation, not an omission: date-picker.css:9-13 states 'Plain calendar surface. No bg/shadow/radius — consumer provides the container (Dialog, Card, or custom wrapper)', and the Docked/InsideDialog stories demonstrate the consumer supplying the surface, header and footer — which is exactly the 'delegation between components' pattern the audit rules say not to flag. The kit sides do check out (Modal Type=Full-screen (range) [360x696] exists; the cell set has Type=Selected (Middle) with Range highlight rects filled Schemes/Secondary Container; Local Actions [360x56] pad=4,12,4,12 gap=8 exists), and DatePickerProps genuinely exposes only value/defaultValue/onChange/minDate/maxDate/className. But an unbuilt range mode is a feature request, and the finding itself concludes 'track this as a deliberate scope decision' — there is nothing actionable to fix against the kit.

ExtendedFab.summary: `.md-extended-fab:hover` (0,2,0) is out-specified by `.md-button[data-variant="filled"]:hover` (0,3,0), so a filled extended FAB drops to elevation level 1 on hover instead of rising to level 4.

ExtendedFab.kitVariant: Buttons / Extended FAB — Size=Small, Color=Primary, State=Enabled vs State=Hovered
ExtendedFab.fix: Raise the selectors' specificity, e.g. `.md-extended-fab[data-variant]` / `.md-extended-fab[data-variant]:hover`, so the FAB elevation wins over Button's per-variant box-shadow rules

verdicts.reason: Kit Enabled shadow = r3 y1 #0000004d + r8 y4 sp3 #00000026, which is exactly --md-sys-elevation-3 (sys.elevation.css:10); Hovered = r3 y2 + r10 y6 sp4 = --md-sys-elevation-4 (line 11). extended-fab.css:9/24-26 set 3 at rest and 4 on hover at specificity (0,1,0)/(0,2,0). button.css:207-213 compiles to `.md-button[data-variant="filled"]:hover` (0,3,0) -> elevation-1, and 217-224 to `.md-button[data-variant="elevated"]` (0,2,0) -> elevation-1 at rest plus (0,3,0) hover -> elevation-2. Higher specificity wins regardless of file order, so a filled EFAB drops 3 -> 1 on hover and an elevated EFAB sits at 1/2. (Default variant is tonal, which has no box-shadow rule and behaves correctly, so this bites the Filled and Elevated stories only.)

Confirmed against the compiled bundle, not just the source. dist/styles/globals.css contains `.md-extended-fab{box-shadow:var(--md-sys-elevation-3)}` (0,1,0), `.md-extended-fab:hover{box-shadow:var(--md-sys-elevation-4)}` (0,2,0), `.md-button[data-variant=filled]:hover{box-shadow:var(--md-sys-elevation-1)}` (0,3,0) and `.md-button[data-variant=elevated]{...box-shadow:var(--md-sys-elevation-1)}` (0,2,0). The element carries both classes (extended-fab.tsx:33 cx('md-extended-fab', className) + button.tsx:48 'md-button'), so for variant="filled" the rest state is elevation-3 but hover resolves to elevation-1 — the shadow visibly DROPS on hover — and variant="elevated" sits at 1/2 instead of 3/4. Kit side verified: every Extended FAB Enabled variant has shadow r3 y1 #0000004d + r8 y4 #00000026 = --md-sys-elevation-3 (0 1px 3px .3 / 0 4px 8px 3px .15) and every Hovered variant r3 y2 + r10 y6 = --md-sys-elevation-4 (0 2px 3px .3 / 0 6px 10px 4px .15). Strongly corroborated as an oversight rather than intent: fab.css:9 uses the compound `.md-icon-button.md-fab` with the literal comment "Compound selector ensures correct specificity vs IconButton base rules" — extended-fab.css never got that guard. Note the default variant (tonal) is unaffected, so only filled (= kit Color=Primary) and elevated misbehave.

ExtendedFab.summary: Only 2 of the kit's 6 extended-FAB colour roles are reachable, and three variants m3you does expose (elevated, outlined, text) have no extended-FAB counterpart in the kit.
ExtendedFab.ours: variant axis inherited from Button: filled (primary/on-primary) = kit Primary, tonal (secondary-container/on-secondary-container) = kit Secondary container, plus elevated/outlined/text
ExtendedFab.kit: Color=[Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Primary container, Secondary container, Tertiary container] — container fill = Schemes/<Role>, label+icon = Schemes/On <Role>; no elevated, outlined or text extended FAB exists
ExtendedFab.kitVariant: Buttons / Extended FAB — Color axis (all 6 values, State=Enabled)
ExtendedFab.fix: Give ExtendedFAB its own `color` axis covering primary/secondary/tertiary and their -container roles rather than reusing Button's emphasis variants

verdicts.reason: Kit Color axis has exactly 6 values (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Primary/Secondary/Tertiary container); container fill=Schemes/<Role>, label+icon fill=Schemes/On <Role> — verified across the dumped variants. m3you reaches only two of those roles: filled = primary/on-primary (button.css:207-210) = kit Primary, tonal = secondary-container/on-secondary-container (button.css:228-231) = kit Secondary container. Secondary, Tertiary, Primary container and Tertiary container are unreachable. The second half of the claim is weaker: a superset is not per se a defect, though `text`/`outlined` EFABs render transparent with no container, which no kit EFAB does.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as a coverage gap: 4 of the kit's 6 EFAB colour roles (Secondary, Tertiary, Primary container, Tertiary container) are unreachable. The 'three extra variants' half is an API-superset observation, not a measured defect.

verdicts.reason: The counts are right but the conclusion is not a defect. Kit Color axis is indeed [Primary|Secondary|Tertiary|Primary container|Secondary container|Tertiary container], and m3you reaches only 2 of them — but the roles it does render are exactly correct (filled = --md-sys-color-primary/on-primary = kit fill=Schemes/Primary + label fill=Schemes/On Primary; tonal = secondary-container/on-secondary-container = kit Secondary container). There is no role mismatch anywhere, only unexposed palette options. Mapping colour onto an emphasis-variant axis is a deliberate, library-wide architectural stance, not an ExtendedFab slip: FAB delegates to IconButton's variants (fab.tsx:14,23), ExtendableFAB re-declares the identical vocabulary (ExtendableFABVariant = 'standard'|'filled'|'elevated'|'tonal'|'outlined'|'text', extendable-fab.tsx:7), and FabMenu hardcodes variant="tonal" (fab-menu.tsx:218). The proposed fix (give ExtendedFAB its own `color` axis and drop elevated/outlined/text) is a breaking API redesign that would desynchronise ExtendedFab from the rest of the FAB family and delete variants that stories and consumers use, so the second half of the claim is actively wrong.

verdicts.reason: extended-fab.css:12-17 compiles to `.md-extended-fab[data-size="sm"]` etc. = (0,2,0); button.css:157-171 gives `.md-button[data-shape="square"][data-size="sm"]` = (0,3,0), and ExtendedFAB always passes shape="square" (extended-fab.tsx:32), so Button always wins. measurements.json confirms: size sm borderRadius "12px" (= corner-medium, sys.shape.css:10) although extended-fab.css:15 declares corner-large (16px); md 16px and lg 28px only match by coincidence with button.css. Dead declarations confirmed. Note the only sizes where the values actually diverge (xs/sm) are sizes the kit does not define, which is why this is correctly rated low.

The mechanics are accurate but there is no kit deviation, so nothing is actionable. Specificity math confirmed in dist/styles/globals.css: `.md-extended-fab[data-size=sm]{border-radius:var(--md-sys-shape-corner-large)}` (0,2,0) loses to `.md-button[data-shape=square][data-size=sm]{border-radius:var(--md-sys-shape-corner-medium)}` (0,3,0), and measurements.json shows borderRadius "12px" for sm. But the resolved radius matches the kit exactly for every size the kit defines: md renders 16px = kit Size=Small r=16 (Corner/Large), lg renders 28px = kit Size=Large r=28 (Corner/Extra-large). The only size where the inert declaration would have changed anything is sm (40px) / xs (32px), and the kit has no 40px or 32px Extended FAB at all — so the "wrong" 12px is a radius on a size that has no kit counterpart. The declarations are redundant, not wrong. The proposed fix also has a cost: raising them to (0,3,0) puts them in a specificity tie with `.md-extended-fab.md-fab-menu-trigger[data-menu-state=open]{border-radius:calc(var(--_height)/2)}` (0,3,0), leaving the FAB-menu collapse morph decided purely by bundle source order.

Reproduced. Kit filled disabled (`Buttons / Icon button — Type=Round, Size=Small, Width=Default, State=Disabled`): Content fill = State Layers/On Surface/Opacity-10@0.1, and the State-layer wrapping the Icon carries opacity=0.38. FabMenu.summary: Segments resolve to a 58px-tall box outside Storybook because .md-button never sets box-sizing:border-box and the UA button padding-block:1px is left in place — measurements.json hides this since Storybook injects Tailwind preflight.
FabMenu.ours: .md-button sets height:56px and padding-inline:24px only; computed padding in measurements.json is "1px 24px", i.e. the UA padding-block survives. With the default content-box, the segment border box is 56+2=58px and the calc(var(--_height)/2)=28px radius leaves a ~1px flat edge instead of a true pill.
FabMenu.fix: Add `box-sizing: border-box;` (and `padding-block: 0;`) to the `.md-button` base rule so the shipped stylesheet is reset-independent.

verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the 58px box does not exist. `<button>` is `box-sizing: border-box` in the UA stylesheet (HTML Standard rendering section), so height:56px + the UA padding-block:1px still yields a 56px border box with no reset at all. I verified empirically in a bare about:blank page with ONLY `.md-button{display:inline-flex;border:none;min-width:58px;height:56px;padding-inline:24px}` injected — no preflight, no globals.css: getComputedStyle → boxSizing "border-box", padding "1px 24px", height "56px", getBoundingClientRect().height = 56, offsetHeight = 56. The secondary claim is also false: Tailwind preflight is never loaded — @tailwindcss/vite is registered in .storybook/main.ts but no CSS file in the repo contains `@import "tailwindcss"` (grepped the whole repo), and .storybook/preview.css / preview-head.html / .design-sync/preview-base.css contain no reset. measurements.json is therefore reset-independent and already proves border-box: `md|outlined` buttons measure height 56 with `padding 1px 24px` AND `border 1px solid` (content-box would give 60), and `lg|outlined` measure 96 with `1px 48px` + `2px solid` (content-box would give 102). The pill radius is exact, not ~1px flat.

Refuted on the premise. (a) Storybook does NOT inject Tailwind preflight: .storybook/main.ts registers tailwindVite() but no CSS entry contains `@import "tailwindcss"` (grep across the repo finds it only in docs/src/styles/app.css, the separate docs site; .storybook/preview.css only sets body font-family). So measurements.json already IS the reset-free, shipped-stylesheet truth — and actions-fab-menu--open reports the items at exactly height 56 with borderRadius 28px, not 58. (b) The reason is that browsers' UA stylesheet already sets box-sizing:border-box on <button>. I verified with Playwright/Chromium on a bare page with zero reset CSS: `<button style='height:56px;padding-inline:24px;border:none'>` → getComputedStyle = {boxSizing:'border-box', padding:'1px 24px'}, getBoundingClientRect().height = 56, offsetHeight = 56. The UA padding-block:1px survives (as the finding says) but is absorbed inside the 56px border box, so there is no 58px box and no ~1px flat edge; calc(--_height/2)=28px is a true pill.

LinearProgress.summary: The wavy indeterminate SVG is stretched non-uniformly, so the rendered wavelength depends on the container width instead of being a fixed 20dp.

Switch.fix: Give .md-switch__state-layer `z-index: 1` (or move it inside the track element after the background) so it paints over the track.

Switch.summary: There is no :focus-visible treatment at all — keyboard focus renders nothing because the only focusable node is the sr-only input.
Switch.ours: switch.css contains no `focus` selector; the tsx puts Tailwind `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` on the track, which is not a focusable element and is not a class the shipped stylesheet defines.
Switch.kit: State=Focused variants add `Focus indicator [56x36] r=100 stroke=Schemes/Secondary w=3` (i.e. 3dp ring, 2dp outside the 52x32 track) plus a 12% state layer.
Switch.fix: Add `.md-switch:has(input:focus-visible) .md-switch__track { outline: 3px solid var(--md-sys-color-secondary); outline-offset: 2px; }` (the sibling Checkbox already uses the `:has(input:focus-visible)` pattern).

Switch.summary: The pressed state is not implemented: no handle grow, no track inset change, no 12% state layer.
Switch.ours: No `:active` / pressed rule exists; the handle stays 18/24px at translateX(8/24px) and the state layer only reacts to :hover.
Switch.kit: State=Pressed: track pad becomes 2,2,2,2, Handle shape grows to 28x28 (offset 2px from the track edge, i.e. translateX(2px) unselected / translateX(22px) selected), State-layer fill 12%.
Switch.fix: Add `.md-switch:active` rules setting the thumb to 28x28 with translateX(2px)/translateX(22px) and the state layer to var(--md-sys-state-pressed-opacity).

Switch.summary: The unselected handle without an icon is 18x18px instead of the kit's 16x16.
Switch.kit: Selected=False, Icon=False → track pad 2,8,2,8, Handle shape [16x16] → 16px thumb inset 8px from the left edge.
Switch.fix: Change width/height to 16px (keep translateX(8px)); switch.tsx:89 already says `size-4` = 16px and the header comment says 16px.

Switch.summary: The handle state layer is 36px and offset ±12px, so it is both undersized and off-centre from the handle.
Switch.ours: width/height 36px (switch.css:29-30) with `transform: translateX(-12px)` unselected / `translateX(12px)` selected (switch.css:39,43); against the 52px track centre that puts its centre at x=14 / x=38.
Switch.kit: State-layer [40x40] r=100, centred on the Handle shape: unselected centre x=16 (8+8), selected centre x=36 (24+12) — i.e. ±10px from the 52px track centre.
Switch.fix: Set width/height to 40px and the transforms to translateX(-10px) / translateX(10px) (Checkbox already uses 40px).
Switch.kitVariant: Switch/Switch — Selected=False, State=Enabled, Icon=False vs Selected=True, State=Enabled, Icon=False

Switch.summary: The handle colour does not change on hover/focus/pressed, so the interactive handle roles are never applied.
Switch.ours: Handle fill is fixed per checked state: `--md-sys-color-on-primary` when selected (switch.css:143), `--md-sys-color-outline` when unselected (switch.css:127,135); no hover/focus/active override exists.
Switch.kit: Hovered/Focused/Pressed change Handle shape fill: Selected → Schemes/Primary Container; Unselected → Schemes/On Surface Variant (Enabled stays On Primary / Outline).
Switch.fix: Add hover/focus-visible/active rules setting the thumb background to var(--md-sys-color-primary-container) when checked and var(--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant) when unchecked.
Switch.kitVariant: Switch/Switch — Selected=True, State=Hovered, Icon=False and Selected=False, State=Hovered, Icon=False

Switch.summary: The unselected hover state layer uses the outline role instead of on-surface.
Switch.kit: Selected=False, State=Hovered: State-layer fill #1f1f1f@0.08 — the unbound legacy on-surface value (selected uses #0b57d0@0.08 = primary, which m3you matches).
Switch.fix: Swap `--md-sys-color-outline` for `--md-sys-color-on-surface` in the unselected state-layer rule.

Switch.summary: Disabled is a blanket 38% opacity on the whole component instead of the kit's per-slot disabled roles.
Switch.ours: `&[data-disabled] { opacity: var(--md-sys-state-disabled-opacity); }` — a disabled selected switch therefore renders a 38%-alpha primary track and a 38% on-primary handle.
Switch.kit: Selected=True/Disabled: track fill on-surface @12%, Handle shape fill Schemes/Surface at full alpha. Selected=False/Disabled: track fill neutral @12%, 2dp stroke on-surface @12%, handle on-surface @38%.
Switch.fix: Replace the blanket opacity with per-slot disabled rules using var(--md-sys-state-disabled-container-opacity) (0.12) for the track/outline and var(--md-sys-state-disabled-opacity) for the handle/icon.
Switch.kitVariant: Switch/Switch — Selected=True, State=Disabled, Icon=False and Selected=False, State=Disabled, Icon=False

Switch.summary: The unselected track stroke is 1.5px and sits 0.5px inside the edge instead of a flush 2px inside stroke.
Switch.ours: `outline: 1.5px solid; outline-offset: -2px;` — the outline occupies the band 0.5px→2px inset, leaving a 0.5px sliver of track background outside it.
Switch.kit: Selected=False track: stroke Schemes/Outline, strokeWeight 2, strokeAlign INSIDE (raw JSON).
Switch.fix: Change to `outline: 2px solid;` (keeping outline-offset: -2px), which resolves to exactly a flush 2px inside stroke.

Switch.summary: The markup carries Tailwind utility classes that the shipped stylesheet does not define, encoding geometry that contradicts switch.css.
Switch.ours: `h-8 w-[52px] rounded-full transition-all duration-300 ease-out focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` on the track (:74), `size-10 rounded-full` on the state layer (:68), `size-6`/`size-4` on the thumb (:89), `opacity-38 pointer-events-none` on the label (:61); Tailwind is Storybook-only per CLAUDE.md and utilities.css defines only `.md-sr-only`, so these are dead in the published package while duplicating/contradicting the CSS (40 vs 36px, 16 vs 18px, 9999px vs 24px radius).
Switch.kit: n/a — repo architecture: variants via data-attributes, all styling in the co-located CSS.
Switch.fix: Delete the Tailwind utilities from switch.tsx and keep the geometry solely in switch.css (`rounded-full` also re-introduces the banned 9999px radius).

Switch.summary: The tests assert Tailwind class names and the wrong thumb size, so they certify behaviour the library does not ship.
Switch.ours: `expect(thumb).toHaveClass('size-4') // 16px` (:75) while the CSS renders 18px; also asserts `rounded-full` (:68), `bg-primary` (:45), `.size-10.rounded-full` (:239) and `focus-visible:ring-2/ring-ring` (:231-232) — the last two claim focus handling that does not exist in any stylesheet.
Switch.kit: n/a — CLAUDE.md: "Tests assert md-* CSS class names and data-* attributes".
Switch.fix: Rewrite the assertions against `md-switch__*` classes and `data-checked`/`data-with-icon`/`data-variant`, and drop the focus-ring test until a real :focus-visible rule exists.

Switch.summary: The component's layout box is 68x48 instead of the kit's 52x32, so a switch reserves 16px more inline space than spec.
Switch.ours: `.md-switch { height: 48px; width: 68px; }` — confirmed rendered as 68x48 in .design-sync/measurements.json for every switch story.
Switch.kit: The Switch component frame is 52x32; the 48x48 Target is an internal frame that overflows the track rather than inflating it.
Switch.fix: Size .md-switch at 52x32 and expand the touch target with an overflowing pseudo-element (or an oversized input) so the layout footprint stays 52x32.

Switch.summary: The track radius is a hardcoded 24px rather than the prescribed calc(height/2).
Switch.ours: `border-radius: 24px;` on a 32px-tall track — the browser clamps it to 16px, so it looks right today but the declared value is meaningless and cannot animate.
Switch.kit: Track r=100 (fully round) → per CLAUDE.md that must be expressed as calc(var(--_height)/2).
